name: call_indirect_table_entry
description: Calls the handler whose address is read from a global table at a fixed negative offset, passing no arguments, then returns. It has no other work of its own.

name: call_indirect_move_handler
description: Calls a handler fetched from a global table at a fixed negative offset, with no arguments, and returns. The only work is that indirect call.

name: call_indirect_draw_handler
description: Calls a handler fetched from a global table at a fixed negative offset, with no arguments, and returns. The only work is that indirect call.

name: call_indirect_wait_handler
description: Calls a handler fetched from a global table at a fixed negative offset, with no arguments, and returns. The only work is that indirect call.

name: call_indirect_setrgb_handler
description: Calls a handler fetched from a global table at a fixed negative offset, with no arguments, and returns. The only work is that indirect call.

name: call_indirect_rectfill_handler
description: Calls a handler fetched from a global table at a fixed negative offset, with no arguments, and returns. The only work is that indirect call.

name: call_indirect_setapen_handler
description: Calls a handler fetched from a global table at a fixed negative offset, with no arguments, and returns. The only work is that indirect call.

name: call_indirect_setbpen_handler
description: Calls a handler fetched from a global table at a fixed negative offset, with no arguments, and returns. The only work is that indirect call.

name: fade_palette_toward_target
description: Steps the red, green and blue components of sixteen palette entries toward target values, setting each entry and waiting between passes. Quoted strings in an argument buffer are also split into a table of pointers, and input and output handles are opened.

name: fade_palette_to_black
description: Decrements the red, green and blue components of sixteen palette entries toward zero, setting each entry and waiting between passes. Each step stops once all entries have reached zero.

name: fade_palette_with_vblank_sync
description: Decrements the colour components of sixteen palette entries toward zero, setting each entry and waiting for two vertical sync points after each row of sixteen.

name: read_then_write_helper_value
description: Reads a value into a local slot through a helper with flag zero, makes two other helper calls, then writes the slot back through the helper with flag one. It returns the value that was written.

name: write_stack_slot_via_helper
description: Passes the address of a stack slot to a helper with flag one, which writes it, then returns. The routine has no other effect.

name: transfer_global_word_by_flag
description: When the flag argument is zero, stores the global word into the location pointed to by the second argument. Otherwise it loads the global word from that location.

name: compute_signed_magnitude_division
description: Divides the first operand by the second using a 32-step restoring loop on absolute values. It returns zero if either operand is zero and negates the quotient when the operands have different signs.

name: shift_global_variable_left
description: Loads a global 32-bit variable, shifts it left by three bits and returns the result. No other operation is performed.

name: forward_argument_twice
description: Takes one 32-bit argument and passes it twice to another routine as both of its arguments. It then returns without further work.

name: allocate_block_from_free_list
description: Walks a free list in a global table for the first block at least as large as the requested count, then unlinks it or splits it and updates the free-count global. If no block fits, it grows the list through a helper and repeats the request once.

name: forward_second_argument_twice
description: Passes its first argument unchanged and its second argument twice to another routine, then returns. No other work is done.

name: insert_or_update_list_node
description: Inserts a block of the given size into an address-ordered free list anchored by a global, linking it in or merging it with an adjacent entry. It returns minus one and undoes the count change when the block would overlap an existing entry.

name: format_value_as_digit_string
description: Converts a numeric value into a fixed-width buffer of decimal digits by repeated scaling, filling leading positions with zero characters. It copies up to twenty characters to the output buffer and stores the digit count through a result pointer.

name: copy_formatted_digits_to_output
description: Builds a digit buffer from a value by scaling it, then copies the formatted digits to the output buffer. The digit count is written to a result pointer.

name: scale_value_into_digit_buffer
description: Repeatedly scales a fixed-point value by powers of two while writing digit characters into a buffer. It then writes the digit count and the output length through pointers.

name: pad_and_copy_digit_buffer
description: Pads the remaining digit positions with zero characters and copies the digit buffer to the destination. It also writes the length word and a sign-state word through pointers.

name: copy_digits_to_output_buffer
description: Copies a run of digit characters from the working buffer to the output buffer, padding with zeros when the source runs out. It stores the final count through a pointer.

name: fill_zero_digits_and_copy
description: Fills a range of digit positions with zero characters, then copies the digits to the output and stores the length. It is used when the value has no significant digits.

name: decrement_loop_until_zero
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter in a loop until it reaches zero, then returns. The loop does no other work on memory or registers.

name: multiply_pair_by_ten
description: Treats its two 32-bit inputs as the high and low words of a 64-bit value and multiplies it by ten using shifts, additions and carry. It returns the 64-bit product.

name: shift_binary_into_decimal_digits
description: Shifts a 64-bit binary value left one bit at a time into a 16-bit decimal accumulator, subtracting ten from any nibble above nine. This converts the binary value to packed decimal digits over 64 iterations.

name: parse_decimal_number_text
description: Parses a decimal number from text by reading an optional sign, integer digits, a decimal point and an optional exponent, while updating a mantissa word. It returns the parsed value and stores status flags through pointers.

name: parse_signed_decimal_text
description: Reads an optional leading minus sign and the integer digits of a decimal number, updating the mantissa and a flag word. It hands the remaining characters to the exponent and fraction handling.

name: parse_decimal_mantissa_digits
description: Accumulates decimal digit characters into a mantissa word by multiplying the running value by ten and adding each digit. It stops at the first non-digit character.

name: parse_fraction_and_exponent
description: Handles the digits after a decimal point and any following exponent marker, updating the scale and sign flags. It then calls the scaling routine for the final value.

name: parse_exponent_and_scale
description: Reads an exponent marker with an optional sign and digits, then applies the exponent to the 64-bit mantissa. It stores the result and a success flag through pointers.

name: normalize_mantissa_by_exponent
description: Applies a decimal exponent to a 64-bit mantissa by repeated doubling or halving until the exponent count reaches zero. It stores the resulting value and a success flag.

name: store_scaled_mantissa_result
description: Negates the exponent when its flag is set, applies it to the mantissa, and stores the 64-bit result and a success flag through pointers.

name: adjust_exponent_until_zero
description: Repeatedly shifts the mantissa one step for each count in the exponent until the count is zero. It then stores the final value and sets the success flag.

name: scale_mantissa_by_exponent_loop
description: Loops over the exponent word, doubling or halving the mantissa word and adjusting the exponent counter until the counter reaches zero. It stores the final mantissa value.

name: store_result_and_success_flag
description: Passes its arguments to another routine, stores the returned 64-bit value through a pointer, and sets a success flag. The value is returned to the caller.

name: decrement_count_and_fetch
description: If a flag word is set, clears it and returns. Otherwise it calls a handler through a pointer, stores the returned word, decrements a countdown and sets a done bit when the countdown reaches zero.

name: fetch_word_and_count_down
description: Calls a handler through a pointer in the context, stores the returned word in the output record, and decrements a countdown. When the countdown reaches zero it sets a done bit in the status word.

name: stub_no_operation_return
description: Returns immediately with no work, so it is an empty stub. The decoded block contains nothing else.

name: check_signal_and_dispatch
description: Reads two signal bits and returns zero if neither is set. When a global flag is nonzero it sends a caret, a one-letter status code and a newline through a helper, then sends each index up to a global count and returns the result of a final two-argument call.

name: open_intuition_library_request
description: Opens the intuition library by name and stores the library pointer in a global. It then shows an automatic requester sized 250 by 40 units and waits for 20 ticks.

name: create_message_port
description: Allocates a signal bit and a 34-byte block, fills in the port fields including the current task, then initialises an empty message list or adds the port to the public list. It releases the signal and returns zero if the allocation fails.

name: delete_message_port
description: Removes the port from the public list when its linked field is nonzero, marks it as deleted, frees its signal bit and releases the 34-byte memory block.

name: dispatch_format_conversion
description: Skips flag characters in a format string, reads an optional length modifier, then fetches the next character through a callback. It dispatches to a conversion handler chosen from a table, or stores minus one and returns zero when the callback reports the end of input.

name: parse_numeric_or_store_char
description: If the current character is a digit, a minus sign or a decimal point, it parses a numeric field through a helper and stores the result. Otherwise it stores the character as is and returns zero.

name: parse_numeric_field_copy_value
description: Parses a numeric field through a helper when the current character is a digit, minus sign or decimal point, then copies the parsed pair of words into the target. It returns the advance count plus one.

name: parse_numeric_field_value
description: Parses a numeric field through a helper, stores the returned value at the target, and records the current position. It returns the advance count plus one.

name: store_format_result_value
description: When the output flag is set, stores a value either by calling a helper or by copying a pair of words through the target pointer. It then writes the current position and returns the advance count plus one.

name: copy_pair_and_advance
description: Copies two 32-bit words from the working record into the target pointer, writes the current position, and returns the advance count plus one.

name: advance_position_by_one
description: Writes the current position into the target pointer and returns one more than the stored count.

name: write_byte_to_stream_buffer
description: Writes one byte into a stream buffer structure, returning minus one if the byte is minus one or the stream is in an error or read-only state. Otherwise it stores the byte at the buffer front or back depending on the mode flags and returns it.

name: stub_immediate_return_only
description: Its body is a bare return with no observable work on data or registers. The decoded instructions do not show any behaviour.

name: divide_unsigned_values_restoring
description: Divides the first unsigned 32-bit value by the second using a 32-step restoring loop. It returns zero if either input is zero.

name: initialise_empty_list
description: Sets up an empty list header in the memory it is given: the head points to the first entry slot, the next word is cleared, and the tail points back to the head.

name: execute_twice
description: Calls another routine twice in succession with no arguments, then returns.

name: store_argument_to_global
description: Copies its one argument into a fixed global variable and returns.

name: unpack_mantissa_with_implied_bit
description: Takes a 64-bit value, moves its top ten bits from the low word into the high word and sets the high word's top bit. A zero input returns zero.

name: shift_sign_bits_to_result
description: Shifts ten bits out of the second input and feeds them into the low bits of the first input. It then sets the top bit of the accumulated result and returns it.

name: normalize_float_and_flag_range
description: Normalises a 64-bit mantissa so its leading bit sits at a fixed position while adjusting an exponent counter. It reports underflow through a helper with code one and overflow with code two.

name: pack_double_precision_result
description: Shifts a mantissa until its top bit is set, adds the exponent bias, and packs the exponent and fraction into the high word. Out-of-range values are reported through a helper and return zero.

name: report_underflow_return_zero
description: Reports code one to a helper and returns a zero double-precision value.

name: report_overflow_return_infinity
description: Reports code two to a helper and returns an infinity value whose sign comes from the high word of the input.

name: shift_left_eight_bits
description: Returns zero for an input whose low 31 bits are clear. Otherwise it shifts the input left eight bits and sets its top bit.

name: normalize_single_precision_mantissa
description: Shifts a 32-bit mantissa until bit 23 is set, adjusting an exponent counter as it goes. It reports underflow through a helper with code one and overflow with code two.

name: pack_single_precision_result
description: Shifts the fraction until its top bit is set, adds the 127 exponent bias, and packs the exponent and fraction into a single-precision word. Out-of-range values report through a helper and return zero or infinity.

name: report_single_underflow_zero
description: Reports code one to a helper and returns zero.

name: report_single_overflow_infinity
description: Reports code two to a helper and returns a single-precision infinity whose sign comes from the input.

name: parse_argument_line_and_open
description: Splits a quoted or space-separated argument line into a table of pointers, then opens a file handle using the current task. It stores the handle and status flags in the global state.

name: compare_strings_up_to_limit
description: Compares two zero-terminated byte strings for at most a given count. It returns the difference of the first mismatching bytes, or one or minus one when one string ends first, and zero when they match.

name: compare_strings_from_context
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings held in a context record, advancing both pointers and decrementing a remaining count. It returns the first byte difference, one or minus one for differing ends, or zero when equal.

name: compare_remaining_string_lengths
description: After a comparison loop ends, returns one if the first string still has characters, minus one if only the second has, and zero when both have ended.

name: check_second_string_remaining
description: Returns minus one if the second string still has characters, otherwise zero.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero without performing any other work.

name: allocate_and_fill_command_buffer
description: Walks a chain of indexed entries to find the largest stored value, allocates a buffer sized from it, and writes a small header with a fill pattern. It copies a sixteen-word block into the buffer and returns minus one on failure.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If the destination pointer is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed working area into it. It then calls a helper through a pointer held in a register and returns.

name: allocate_and_fill_command_buffer
description: Walks a chain of indexed entries to find the largest stored value, allocates a buffer sized from it, and writes a small header with a fill pattern. It copies a sixteen-word block into the buffer and returns minus one on failure.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If the destination pointer is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed working area into it. It then calls a helper through a pointer held in a register and returns.

name: allocate_and_fill_command_buffer
description: Walks a chain of indexed entries to find the largest stored value, allocates a buffer sized from it, and writes a small header with a fill pattern. It copies a sixteen-word block into the buffer and returns minus one on failure.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If the destination pointer is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed working area into it. It then calls a helper through a pointer held in a register and returns.

name: run_event_dispatch_loop
description: Clears a range of table entries to zero and writes a fixed tag word, then loops over an event code and compares it against a list of fixed codes. Each matched case calls one or more helpers before the loop continues.

name: build_command_line_from_task
description: Finds the current task and reads its command record, then copies an argument string into a stack buffer followed by a separator and the name from the record. It passes the buffer to a helper and sets up the library state.

name: release_handles_and_return
description: If a stored handle is set, releases two resource handles through library calls, then calls the shutdown vector. It returns the value it was given.

name: invoke_two_function_pointers
description: Calls two library vector entries at fixed negative offsets from a base register, one after the other, and then returns.

name: open_dos_library_or_fail
description: Opens the dos library through the exec vector and stores its base. If opening fails it runs the release sequence and returns one hundred; otherwise it returns the library base.

name: allocate_memory_block
description: Calls the exec AllocMem vector through the stored library base, passing the caller's arguments through, and returns the result.

name: free_memory_block
description: Calls the exec FreeMem vector through the stored library base, passing the caller's arguments through.

name: find_current_task
description: Calls the exec FindTask vector through the stored library base and returns the task pointer.

name: set_signal_bits
description: Calls the exec SetSignal vector through the stored library base, passing the caller's arguments through.

name: open_named_library
description: Calls the exec OpenLibrary vector through the stored library base, passing the caller's arguments through.

name: parse_string_table
description: Splits a null-terminated command line into tokens at spaces or double quotes, storing a pointer to each token in a table and terminating tokens in place. A non-terminated quoted string is reported as an error. With no tokens it opens the dos library and finds the current task; otherwise it obtains input and output handles and opens a file.

name: allocate_and_init_block
description: Allocates a memory block of the requested size plus twelve bytes, records the total size inside the block, and passes the block to a helper with a global pointer. It returns the address just past the header.

name: allocate_block_or_minus_one
description: Passes its argument to the allocation routine and returns the resulting block address. It returns minus one when that result is zero.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one and performs no other work.

name: free_linked_memory_blocks
description: Walks a singly linked list whose head is a global variable. For each node it frees the node using the size stored in the node, then follows the next pointer until the list is empty.

name: append_node_to_list
description: Appends a new node to a list whose header holds the head and tail pointers. It copies the old tail into the new node, links the previous tail forward to the new node, and sets the head if the list was empty.

name: expand_format_string
description: Copies a percent-escaped format string to an output destination, emitting a single percent sign for a doubled percent. Conversion specifiers are expanded through a helper into a local buffer, and each output byte is written through the destination pointer or a callback when the buffer is full.

name: fill_global_table_entries
description: Stores twenty values from a helper into successive entries of a global table, then calls a helper once for each index up to a stored count. It finishes by calling a final helper with the two arguments it received.

name: copy_string_to_offset
description: Calls a helper with its first argument, then copies a zero-terminated string from the second argument into memory starting at the returned offset plus the first argument. It returns the first argument unchanged.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a buffer computed from the first argument and a helper result, stopping at a zero byte or when a length counter runs out. It writes a terminating zero and returns the first argument.

name: open_dos_file
description: Calls the dos Open vector through the stored dos library base, passing the caller's arguments, and returns the handle.

name: close_dos_file
description: Calls the dos Close vector through the stored dos library base and returns.

name: read_dos_file
description: Calls the dos Read vector through the stored dos library base, passing the caller's arguments through.

name: write_dos_file
description: Calls the dos Write vector through the stored dos library base, passing the caller's arguments through.

name: get_dos_input_handle
description: Calls the dos Input vector through the stored dos library base and returns the current input handle.

name: get_dos_output_handle
description: Calls the dos Output vector through the stored dos library base and returns the current output handle.

name: seek_dos_file
description: Calls the dos Seek vector through the stored dos library base, passing the caller's arguments through.

name: delete_dos_file
description: Calls the dos DeleteFile vector through the stored dos library base, passing the caller's arguments through.

name: rename_dos_file
description: Calls the dos Rename vector through the stored dos library base, passing the caller's arguments through.

name: read_dos_error_code
description: Calls the dos IoErr vector through the stored dos library base and returns the last DOS error code.

name: read_numeric_records_from_file
description: Prompts for file and record numbers, then reads up to 400 records of numeric fields through a formatted-input helper. Each record is stored in a buffer and written out through a formatted-output helper.

name: read_next_buffered_byte
description: Returns the next byte from a buffered stream structure, calling a helper to refill the buffer when it is empty. It returns minus one when the stream is in an error or end state.

name: write_byte_to_buffered_stream
description: Writes one byte into a buffered stream structure, flushing through a helper when the buffer is full. It sets error bits in the state byte when a write fails and retries through a recursive call when the counter underflows.

name: open_stream_buffer_or_fail
description: If the stream already holds a buffer it returns zero. Otherwise it obtains a new buffer through a helper and resets the state and count fields. When the allocation fails it stores error code twelve and returns minus one.

name: dispatch_numeric_format_spec
description: Skips an optional minus sign, digits, a decimal point and a long-size marker in a format string. It then looks up the remaining character in a table and calls the matching handler, returning zero when no entry matches.

name: format_number_with_padding
description: Writes a formatted number into the output buffer with an optional minus sign, padding with spaces or zeros to the requested width. It places the integer digits, a decimal point and fraction digits in order.

name: emit_formatted_number_digits
description: Emits the digit characters of a formatted number into the output buffer, adding a decimal point and an exponent with its sign when required. Exponents above ninety-nine and nine hundred ninety-nine add extra digit positions.

name: pad_and_emit_number_text
description: Pads a formatted number to its field width, then emits the sign, digits and exponent text into the output buffer through the output pointer or a callback.

name: emit_padding_characters
description: Writes a run of fill characters into the output buffer for a computed count, then stores the updated output position. It is a plain padding step with no digit handling.

name: emit_padding_then_digits
description: Writes padding characters followed by a run of characters from the source buffer into the output. It stores the updated output position when finished.

name: copy_source_characters_to_output
description: Copies a counted run of bytes from the source buffer to the output buffer and stores the final output position. The copy stops when the count runs out.

name: copy_value_and_increment_counter
description: Stores a saved value into the output record and returns the stored count plus one. It performs a single store and a single addition.

name: format_fixed_or_exponent_number
description: Works out the digit counts for a floating-point value and chooses between fixed-point and exponent layout. It then emits the digits, decimal point and any exponent, padding the field to its width.

name: format_scientific_number_layout
description: Emits a leading digit and fraction digits for a scientific-notation layout, followed by an exponent marker, its sign and two or three exponent digits. Padding is applied to the field width afterwards.

name: format_number_with_zero_fraction
description: Writes a zero integer part, a decimal point and fraction digits when the exponent is negative. Otherwise it emits the integer and fraction digits, adds an exponent when required, and pads the field.

name: emit_exponent_and_fraction_digits
description: Adds the exponent width to the field, emits padding and an optional sign, then writes the integer digits, decimal point and fraction digits followed by the exponent marker.

name: emit_exponent_with_padding
description: Checks the exponent digit counts, pads the field with fill characters, and writes the minus sign and mantissa digits. It then writes the exponent parts.

name: emit_decimal_number_body
description: Writes an optional minus sign and the integer digits, followed by a decimal point or an exponent section. It then pads the field to its width and stores the output count.

name: emit_digits_and_pad_field
description: Emits digit characters from a working buffer into the output, filling with zeros once the buffer runs out. It pads the remaining field width when the padding flag is set and stores the output count.

name: emit_zero_digits_with_padding
description: Writes a zero digit, then the remaining digit characters from the working buffer, and pads the field to its width. It stores the output count.

name: emit_integer_and_fraction_digits
description: Emits the integer digits, a decimal point when a flag is set, then the fraction digits and any remaining field padding. It stores the output count.

name: emit_zero_padded_fraction
description: Writes zero characters for the integer part, adds a decimal point when a flag is set, then emits fraction digits and pads to width.

name: emit_fraction_digits_and_pad
description: Writes the decimal point when a flag is set, emits the remaining digits, pads the field with fill characters, and stores the output count.

name: emit_zero_and_pad_field
description: Emits a zero digit and the remaining digits from the working buffer, then pads to the field width using the fill byte and stores the output count.

name: emit_scientific_exponent_notation
description: Writes one leading digit, a decimal point and the mantissa digits, then the exponent marker, its sign and the exponent digits. It pads the field to its width.

name: emit_scientific_zero_mantissa
description: Writes a zero integer digit and a decimal point, then mantissa digits and an exponent with its sign, followed by padding.

name: emit_exponent_with_digit_loop
description: Writes zero digits to the mantissa, then the exponent marker, sign and digits, padding to the field width.

name: emit_exponent_suffix_and_pad
description: Writes the exponent marker, its sign and the exponent digits, then pads the remaining field width and stores the output count.

name: emit_exponent_sign_digits
description: Writes a plus sign and the exponent digits from the working buffer into the output. It then fills the field and stores the output count.

name: emit_padding_and_store_count
description: Writes fill characters into the output when the padding flag is set, then stores the output count and returns the advance count plus one.

name: copy_value_and_increment_counter
description: Stores a saved value into the output record and returns the stored count plus one. It performs a single store and a single addition.

name: empty_stub_function
description: Returns immediately with no effect on memory, registers or I/O.

name: find_free_entry_and_call
description: Scans a table of 24-byte entries for one whose flag byte is clear. It returns zero when the table is full, otherwise it passes the free entry and the two arguments to a helper.

name: call_helper_unless_at_end
description: Returns zero when the scanned pointer has reached the end of the table, otherwise calls a helper with the two stored arguments and the pointer.

name: forward_entry_arguments
description: Passes the two stored arguments and the table entry pointer to a helper, then returns.

name: open_file_with_mode_string
description: Parses a mode string containing r, w or a and optional b and plus characters. It calls a helper to open the file with the matching access flags and a permission value, and returns zero on failure.

name: open_stream_record_for_mode
description: Parses the same kind of mode string as its neighbour, opens the file through a helper, and fills in a stream record. It returns the record, or zero when the open fails.

name: open_append_stream_record
description: Opens a file with the flags it was given and a permission value, seeks to the end, then initialises a stream record and returns it.

name: seek_end_init_record
description: Seeks to the end of the open file, stores the state byte, initialises the stream record and returns it.

name: init_stream_record_state_two
description: Stores state two in the record, clears its buffer fields and returns the record. No file operation is performed.

name: open_file_init_record
description: Opens the file with a read or read-write access flag, stores the handle and state, initialises the stream record and returns it. It returns zero when the open fails.

name: open_handle_and_init_stream
description: Calls a helper with two arguments to obtain a handle, stores the handle and state, then initialises the stream record. It returns zero when the handle is invalid.

name: init_stream_record_state_one
description: Stores a state byte of one or a flagged state in the record, clears its buffer fields, and returns the record.

name: init_stream_record_plain_one
description: Stores state one in the record, marks it buffered when a helper reports a buffer, initialises the fields and returns the record.

name: open_new_stream_with_mode
description: Opens a file with create and write flags and a permission value, stores the handle and state, then initialises the stream record and returns it.

name: open_create_stream_record
description: Opens a file with a write and create flag combination and a permission value, stores the handle and state, initialises the stream record and returns it.

name: init_stream_record_mode_flag
description: Stores a state byte chosen by a mode flag in the record, initialises its fields and returns it.

name: init_record_state_two_alt
description: Stores state two in the record, clears its buffer fields and returns the record. It is the same record setup as its neighbour.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero without performing any other work.

name: finish_stream_record_setup
description: Stores the handle state byte in the record, initialises its fields and returns the record. Its flag selects whether the buffer is marked as in use.

name: clear_stream_record_fields
description: Clears the record's count word, sets its buffer fields and state byte, then returns the record.

name: clear_object_links
description: Checks the flag byte of an object and, when the link bit is clear and a pointer field is set, passes the stored values to a helper. It then clears the two pointer fields and the flag byte, and calls a helper with a byte taken from the structure.

name: check_flag_and_return_pointer
description: Checks that the index lies within the table bounds and tests a flag bit in a global table. When the bit is set it returns a pointer to a second table entry; otherwise it records error code nine and returns null.

name: open_file_and_set_flags
description: Finds a free slot in a global table, sets flag bits in that slot from the mode argument, and deletes the file first when requested. It opens the file with the dos Open vector and stores the handle, recording the I/O error and returning minus one on failure.

name: set_open_flags_and_call
description: Builds two flag words from its second argument and passes them with the first argument to another routine. It then returns.

name: read_with_error_handling
description: Looks up the stream for the handle, reads the requested number of bytes through the dos Read vector, and records the I/O error and an error code when the read fails. It returns minus one for an invalid length or handle.

name: write_handle_checked
description: Looks up the handle, seeks to the end first when the append flag is set, and writes the buffer through the dos Write vector. It records the I/O error and returns minus one for an invalid handle or length.

name: seek_file_with_offset_table
description: Looks up the handle and seeks the file to an offset taken from a global table indexed by the third argument. It records an I/O error if that seek fails, then seeks back to the start and returns the result.

name: close_handle_if_flag_clear
description: Looks up the handle slot and returns minus one for a null slot. If the no-close flag is set it returns zero; otherwise it closes the handle through the dos Close vector, clears the slot's state byte and returns zero.

name: delete_file_with_error_check
description: Deletes the named file through the dos DeleteFile vector. On failure it records the I/O error, sets error code two and returns minus one; otherwise it returns zero.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero without performing any other work.

name: open_global_file_handle
description: Opens the named file in a fixed mode through the dos Open vector and stores the returned handle in a global variable.

name: read_byte_with_pushback
description: Returns a byte previously pushed back into a global variable and clears it. Otherwise it reads one byte from the open file handle through the dos Read vector and returns it.

name: read_one_byte_from_handle
description: Reads a single byte from the global file handle through the dos Read vector into a stack slot and returns that byte.

name: write_byte_to_handle
description: Writes one byte to the global file handle through the dos Write vector, calling helpers first when the handle is not yet open. It returns the byte.

name: set_pushback_byte_once
description: Stores its argument as the pushed-back byte when none is pending. Otherwise it returns minus one.

name: store_argument_byte_to_global
description: Stores the low byte of its argument into a global byte variable and returns.

name: close_active_handles
description: Loops over the table entries up to the stored count, closing each open handle that does not have the no-close flag set. It then calls a helper with the original arguments.

name: count_string_bytes
description: Counts the bytes before the first zero byte in a string starting at the given address and returns that count.

name: emit_formatted_string_output
description: Walks a percent-escaped format string, writing each literal byte and each expanded conversion to the output, and collapsing a doubled percent sign to one. It finishes with an end-of-output call.

name: match_format_against_input
description: Matches a format string against an input stream one character at a time, skipping whitespace and reading percent conversions through helpers. It returns the number of successful conversions, or minus one when none were made.

name: read_input_byte
description: Returns the next input byte from the buffer pointer, or calls a helper to refill the buffer when it is empty.

name: push_back_input_state
description: Passes the global input state to a helper and then returns. It does not change any value itself.

name: shift_global_variable_left
description: Loads a global 32-bit variable, shifts it left by three bits and returns the result. No other operation is performed.

name: forward_argument_twice
description: Takes one 32-bit argument and passes it twice to another routine as both of its arguments. It then returns without further work.

name: allocate_block_from_free_list
description: Walks a free list in a global table for the first block at least as large as the requested count, then unlinks it or splits it and updates the free-count global. If no block fits, it grows the list through a helper and repeats the request once.

name: forward_second_argument_twice
description: Passes its first argument unchanged and its second argument twice to another routine, then returns. No other work is done.

name: insert_or_update_list_node
description: Inserts a block of the given size into an address-ordered free list anchored by a global, linking it in or merging it with an adjacent entry. It returns minus one and undoes the count change when the block would overlap an existing entry.

name: format_value_as_digit_string
description: Converts a numeric value into a fixed-width buffer of decimal digits by repeated scaling, filling leading positions with zero characters. It copies up to twenty characters to the output buffer and stores the digit count through a result pointer.

name: copy_formatted_digits_to_output
description: Builds a digit buffer from a value by scaling it, then copies the formatted digits to the output buffer. The digit count is written to a result pointer.

name: scale_value_into_digit_buffer
description: Repeatedly scales a fixed-point value by powers of two while writing digit characters into a buffer. It then writes the digit count and the output length through pointers.

name: pad_and_copy_digit_buffer
description: Pads the remaining digit positions with zero characters and copies the digit buffer to the destination. It also writes the length word and a sign-state word through pointers.

name: copy_digits_to_output_buffer
description: Copies a run of digit characters from the working buffer to the output buffer, padding with zeros when the source runs out. It stores the final count through a pointer.

name: fill_zero_digits_and_copy
description: Fills a range of digit positions with zero characters, then copies the digits to the output and stores the length. It is used when the value has no significant digits.

name: decrement_loop_until_zero
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter in a loop until it reaches zero, then returns. The loop does no other work on memory or registers.

name: multiply_pair_by_ten
description: Treats its two 32-bit inputs as the high and low words of a 64-bit value and multiplies it by ten using shifts, additions and carry. It returns the 64-bit product.

name: shift_binary_into_decimal_digits
description: Shifts a 64-bit binary value left one bit at a time into a 16-bit decimal accumulator, subtracting ten from any nibble above nine. This converts the binary value to packed decimal digits over 64 iterations.

name: parse_decimal_number_text
description: Parses a decimal number from text by reading an optional sign, integer digits, a decimal point and an optional exponent, while updating a mantissa word. It returns the parsed value and stores status flags through pointers.
